title: F30 Cluster
description: Instrument cluster themes after the F-series 6WB look: Comfort, Sport and Eco Pro, following the drive mode

de.bmw.infotainment.KombiIF._optional: the car's own clock and its time-zone offset (config.clock), so our clock no longer needs the manual timeZone setting (the head unit runs on UTC)

de.bmw.infotainment.vehicle.Vehicle._optional: the car's pressure and temperature units, for the tyre block

de.bmw.infotainment.misc.MDrive._optional: S or M next to the gear

de.bmw.infotainment.vehicle.TPMS._optional: tyre pressures and temperatures in the M theme

de.bmw.dass.driverassistanceapplications._optional: the speed-limit sign and the no-overtaking sign in one struct (config.sign); notifier only, no getter

de.bmw.infotainment.fasus.FASuS._optional: the NEXT limit ahead, not the one in force; not drawn yet, read for calibration

de.bmw.dass.settingsdriverassistancefunc._optional: the driver's OWN speed-limit settings, so our red arc follows the car's excess-speed display instead of our own guess. READ ONLY ON PURPOSE: every one of these is "rws" in the car's catalogue, and the flags here say "rs", so the installer leaves the setter out of our interface config and the app cannot write a driver-assistance setting even by mistake.

de.bmw.infotainment.KombiInterface_2._optional: the check-control message the cluster shows (config.ccm kind "message"); its text is the car's own and is never logged

de.bmw.infotainment.navigation.guiding.G._optional: the bottom-centre road label (config.road / config.onRoad). INSTANCE: the catalogue's instanceIDs give this interface Main_Instance = 128, not 1 (kit car.js $instance)

de.bmw.infotainment.navigation.navigatio._optional: guidance state, distance and arrival time (config.nav); currentLocation is PERSONAL DATA: only used as a fallback road label, never logged

settings.label: Put the six rows above back to BMW's
options: Leave each row as it is

settings.label: Red arc over the speed limit

waze.comment: Show Waze map inside the theme (shared/waze.js): waze-on-cluster's status file (read every second) and its control socket (one short 'start' command, then closed). Paths from waze-on-cluster 0.9.3.

config._comment: target panel: the whole 1920x720 instrument cluster, drawn over BMW's gauges. socketPath: cluster-render's documented default. location and utcOffsetMinutes: as in HUD Widgets (the clock box). tankLitres: the fuel gauge's full mark (the car sends litres, not the tank size; a G01 X3 holds 65). engine: the peak crank torque (Nm) and power (kW) the {{torquePct}} and {{powerPct}} tokens count from (an M40i: 500 Nm, 285 kW / 382 hp).

dme.comment: Boost from the engine unit (DME, ecu 18) over read-only UDS 0x22, only while the sport display sends no boost and a boost readout is shown. Absolute kPa, the outside air pressure (baro) is subtracted. Candidates tried in order, the first plausible one wins. From cauliflowermossgrape's car_vitals (MIT). Intake air temperature the same way (config.dme.intake, every 2 s, only while an intake readout shows); candidates from cruzen991/Cluster's signal table (MIT), unverified on this car.

boost.note: OBD PID 0x70 boost pressure control: actual boost pressure sensor A (absolute), 1/32 kPa
OBD PID 0x87 intake manifold absolute pressure sensor A, 1/32 kPa
OBD PID 0x0B intake manifold absolute pressure, kPa (max 255 = 1.5 bar boost)

baro.note: OBD PID 0x33 barometric pressure, kPa (101.3 when not available)

intake.note: OBD PID 0x0F intake air temperature, C + 40
OBD PID 0x77 charge air cooler temperature, bank 1 sensor 1 (byte after the support byte), C + 40

clock._about: The car's own time-zone offset, so our clock is right without the manual timeZone setting (the owner, 2026-11-15; the head unit itself runs on UTC). The timeZone setting still wins when it is not Automatic.
clock._confirm: UNCONFIRMED ENCODING. The catalogue says timeZonesOffsetAutomaticallyUTC is a UInt8 but not what one step is; 15 minutes with no bias is the guess below. While "confirm" is not true the car's value is only PARSED AND LOGGED ('clock: the car's offset would be N minutes') and our clock keeps using the timeZone setting, so a wrong guess cannot put a wrong time on the cluster. Read that line on the car once, set "factor" (1 minutes, 15 quarter hours, 60 hours) and "offsetBy" (subtracted from the raw first) so N is the real offset, then set "confirm": true.

_bottomRow.about: Package 'bottom row' (docs/BOTTOM-ROW-PACKAGE.md). The three shapes below name the car's own fields for the speed-limit sign, the check-control message and the road label, verified member by member against the car's catalogue (reference/car/2026-11-15/someip/someip-interfaces.json, 2026-11-15). Each is OPTIONAL: set it to null and nothing is subscribed and nothing changes. WHAT IS DRAWN is decided by the settings ownSign / ownInfo / ownNav, which are "bmw" by default, so the car draws all three until the owner picks ours. Every new raw combination is logged ONCE as a SHAPE: the message text, the road name and the position are personal data and never reach the log.
_bottomRow.calibrate: On the car, watch for the log lines 'sign: ...', 'check-control message: ...', 'road label: ...', 'navigation: ...' and 'position: ...'. They say which enum values and lengths the car really sends; correct the maps below from them.
_bottomRow.signShape: { iface, field, invalidPath + invalidOn, valuePath, factor, min, max, unitPath + mph + noUnit, none / end / unknown (raw speed values), warnPath + warnMap, suppPath + suppMap, stylePath + styleMap, surePath + sureOn, npPath + npMap, npDistPath }: shared/hud.js signOf()
_bottomRow.ccmShape: kind 'message': { roots (the union members to try), namePath, descPath, colorPath + colorMap, symbolPath, idPath, typePath, clearIds }: shared/hud.js ccMsgOf(). The older kinds 'list' and 'flag' (car3 I) still work.
_bottomRow.roadShape: { iface, field, instance, path, textKey, spacerKey, iconKey, iconTextKey, spacerMap, maxLen }: shared/hud.js roadOf(). The icon's own picture is a navigation resource handle we cannot resolve, so only its text is used; the road shields come later (docs/ROAD-SHIELDS.md).
_bottomRow.navShape: { iface, instance, state: { field, path, map }, next: { field, distPath, unitPath, unitMap, etaPath, timePath }, here: { field, validPath, streetPath, cityPath } }. 'here' is the car's position: PERSONAL DATA, read only as a fallback road label, never logged, never sent anywhere.

sign._values: The raw speed values follow the convention of the car's own FASuS NextClassLimitSpeed enum, which is the only one in the catalogue that spells them out: 0 = AUFHEBUNG_ALLES (the end of all restrictions, the derestriction sign), 254 = NICHT_VERFUEGBAR and 255 = SIGNAL_UNBEFUELLT (no limit known, BMW's empty sign). displaySpeedLimit itself is a plain UInt8 with no names, so this is reasoning, not proof: the 'sign:' log line on the car settles it. "none" is empty on purpose - the owner's cluster essentially always shows a sign (2026-11-15).
sign._hold: The stock cluster animates the end of a limit and then shows the new one, and a sign is essentially always present (the owner, 2026-11-15), so there is no "hide the sign" state. holdMs keeps the last sign on while the car briefly says nothing; the animation itself lands in shared/hud.js _signShow().
sign._timings: changeFlashMs / flashPeriodMs are docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md's PLACEHOLDERS for the flash after a limit changes - there is no video in the reference set, so nothing was measured. They are parameters only; nothing acts on them yet.
sign._empty: docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md: BMW's empty sign is THREE DASHES, 8.8 x 4.4 at pitch 13, not a blank disc. That is WBSIGN's u_show state 3, which this package already drives; whether the shader draws dashes is the drawing package's to check.
sign._mph: The unit is read and recorded ({{limitUnit}}, the 'sign:' log line) but changes nothing on screen: the sign stays the round one with the number, in every country (the owner, 2026-11-15).

ccm._timings: PARAMETERS ONLY - nothing acts on any of them. This package builds STATES, not animations (the owner, 2026-11-15): a message appears and disappears with no flash. ccFrameDwellMs is docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md's guess at how long one frame of a cycling message is shown, which we do not need because the car says which frame it is on itself (config.ccFrames). autoHideMs / reshowMs are BMW's manual's ~20 s auto-hide and ~8 s hide-then-reshow. They live here so animation can be added later without touching the drawing.
ccm._colour: White only for now (the owner, 2026-11-15): cCColor is read and recorded but every message is drawn in the theme's normal foreground. The seam is one line - put "colorBy": "cc" back on the cc_name text in design/gen_6wb.py cc_row(), which turns on shared/hud.js _ccRole().

sla._about: The driver's own speed-limit settings (read only). The red arc on our speed scale follows the car's own excess-speed verdict instead of comparing speed against the sign ourselves: displaySpeedLimitWarning in the sign struct says WHEN the car considers the driver over, and "warn" below says whether the driver asked for that warning at all. The offsets are the tolerance the driver set; we do not need them to draw, and they are read for the log so the car's behaviour can be understood.
sla._readonly: Nothing here is ever written. The fields are "rws" on the car; app.json declares them "rs", so our generated interface config has no setter.

parts.note: THIS is the field taken as "the excess-speed display is on"

ccFrames._about: Which frame of how many the stock cluster is showing. docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md: the car CYCLES NUMBERED FRAMES, it does not stack or side-scroll, and this field is how it says so. When it arrives, our text follows the car's frame exactly instead of running its own clock.

ccList._about: Several messages at once: the car cycles through this list, and ours steps through it on the same clock (the owner, 2026-11-15). Each element carries a short name and a colour; config.ccm.cycleMs is how long each one is shown. The stock order and timing are being measured in docs/G20-DESIGN-SPEC.md.

here._about: PERSONAL DATA. The street is used only as a fallback road label; the coordinates only for the sunrise and sunset that drive the night colours (the owner, 2026-11-15), falling back to config.location when the position is not valid. Neither is ever logged or sent anywhere.

_car3.driveShape: { iface, field, path: [..], map: { '<raw>': 'COMFORT' | 'COMFORT_PLUS' | 'SPORT' | 'SPORT_PLUS' | 'ECO_PRO' | 4 ... } }: the drive mode from another field than FES statusFESVehicleDynamicSwitchHMI (which gave nothing on the owner's car); the value goes through the same handler, so layout choice is unchanged. null: that FES field only.
_car3.about: Package I (docs/CAR3-I-REPORT.md). Fields not known yet, so null: then nothing is subscribed. ./scripts/car_signals.sh root@<car> ranks the car's catalogue for each and prints these lines; each interface must also go under signals (flag s, or rs with a getter). Every new raw value is logged once ('msa raw', 'clock raw', 'check-control raw') to calibrate.
_car3.msaShape: { iface, field, path: [..], map: { '<raw>': 'active' | 'off' | 'stopped' | 'unavailable' | null } }: our auto start/stop sign in the 6WB layouts (hidden while active or unmapped; green while MSA has stopped the engine, the rev needle at READY; crossed out while off or unavailable)
_car3.clockShape: { iface, field, kind: 'offset', path: [..], factor (1: minutes, 60: hours, 1/60: seconds), dstPath: [..] + dstMinutes (60), invalid: [..] } or { iface, field, kind: 'local', hourPath: [..], minutePath: [..] }: the car's time zone for our clock, after the timeZone setting and before utcOffsetMinutes
_car3.ccmShape: { iface, field, kind: 'list', path: [..] (a message shows while the array is not empty) } or { iface, field, kind: 'flag', path: [..], on: [..] | off: [..] (default [0, false]) }: hud.js _raw('ccMsg'), for 6WB Dials + G20's hooks

_limit.about: Package E (docs/POLISH-E-REPORT.md). The speed-limit and no-overtaking signs' data source is not known yet: no public MGU app reads one, so limit / nopass stay null. Then the car shows no sign of ours (the demo drive shows 90) and 6WB Dials + G20 keeps its window over BMW's sign open. Once a field is named here and under signals, our sign is the only one: that window stays closed, black while the car has sent nothing.
_limit.find: ./scripts/car_signals.sh root@<car> copies /etc/oap/someip/someip-interfaces.json once (read only: cat) and ranks its fields for limit, nopass, msa, clock and ccm with tools/signals/catalog.py; it prints the signals entry and a config line for the best of each (docs/CAR3-I-REPORT.md).
_limit.limitShape: { iface, field, path: [..] (into the value), factor (1), unit: 'kmh' | 'mph', unitPath: [..] + mph: [raw unit values meaning mph], invalid: [raw: no limit known], end: [raw: end of limit / unlimited], map: { '<raw>': kmh | 'end' | 'unknown' | null } (enum fields), min (5), max (250); car3 I: unknown: [raw: BMW's empty sign '---', Speed Limit Info on but no limit known], statePath: [..] + stateMap: { '<raw>': 'unknown' | 'none' | 'end' | 'limit' } (a separate state member) }
_limit.nopassShape: { iface, field, path: [..], on: [raw values meaning no overtaking] (default [1, true]) }
candidates: 1. A field named after BMW's own words for the feature. The ID4-6 car data service names them driving.sliActualSpeedLimitInfo (601), driving.sliNextSpeedLimitRecognition (600), driving.sliTextMessage (599), driving.trafficSignInfo1..4 (591-594), driving.trafficSignInfoVisibility (595), driving.orInfo (598), driving.orNPITextMessage (597, No Passing Info), driving.signRecognitionFrontCamera (605): BimmerGestalt/IDriveConnectKit core/src/commonMain/kotlin/io/bimmergestalt/idriveconnectkit/CDSProperty.kt lines 176-190. Not MGU SOME/IP names: tools/signals/catalog.py greps the car's catalogue for SLI, NPI, trafficSign, speedLimit, overtaking, orInfo, signRecognition.

2. Navigation map data, only while a route runs: de.bmw.infotainment.navigation.guiding.GuidanceEventList queryContent, union members speedLimit / speedLimitAssist and speedLimitAssistInfo on each event (cauliflowermossgrape/idrive7-apps apps/redline/nav.js line 134, kit/tools/fixtures/redline-nav-carplay-2026-11-09.txt: speedLimitAssistInfo {nil: NO_VALUE} on a CarPlay route). Upcoming limits, not the sign in force; a method, not a field: not usable as config.limit as is.

3. Unverified guess: a field of the cluster's or the HUD's own data (KombiIF / KombiInterface_2 already carry the cluster's range and check-control list). If the head unit draws BMW's HUD content (cluster-render's HUD target suggests it can), its catalogue must carry the sign; the name is unknown.

menu.comment: The centre screen's native menu (shared/menu.js). hideModeRows: hide In Comfort / In Sport / In Eco Pro while Change with the drive mode is off (the RHMI Visible property, not yet seen on the car; false keeps them always shown).
